def find_fault_intervals(df, time_col, elapsed_col, threshold):
    # Sort by time
    df = df.sort_values(time_col).reset_index(drop=True)
    # Identify rows where elapsedTime exceeds threshold
    df['exceed'] = df[elapsed_col] > threshold
    # Identify consecutive intervals where exceed is True
    df['group'] = (df['exceed'] != df['exceed'].shift()).cumsum()
    # Filter groups where exceed is True
    fault_groups = df[df['exceed']].groupby('group')
    # For each group, get start time, end time, and max elapsedTime
    intervals = fault_groups.agg(
        start_time=(time_col, 'first'),
        end_time=(time_col, 'last'),
        max_elapsedTime=(elapsed_col, 'max')
    ).reset_index(drop=True)
    return intervals

# Find fault intervals for docker_002

both_appear = []
downstream_component = []

for trace_id, group in grouped:
    # Sort spans by startTime
    group_sorted = group.sort_values('startTime')
    # Components in this trace
    components = set(group_sorted['cmdb_id'].dropna().unique()).union(set(group_sorted['dsName'].dropna().unique()))
    # Check if both docker_002 and db_007 appear
    has_docker_002 = 'docker_002' in components
    has_db_007 = 'db_007' in components
    both = has_docker_002 and has_db_007
    # Determine which component is most downstream (last in call chain)
    # Use pid to find parent-child relationships
    # The last span is the one with no children (no other span has its id as pid)
    ids = group_sorted['id'].tolist()
    pids = group_sorted['pid'].tolist()
    # Find spans that are not parent of any other span (no id in pid list)

    # Determine downstream component priority: if both appear, note both; else note which one appears
